references.sentence: A block diagram of the CDC is shown in Fig. 11.2.1.
As shown in Fig. 11.2.2, the modulator employs a feed-forward topology.
As shown in Fig. 11.2.3, the modulator’s 3rd-order noise shaping ensures that with a 5MHz clock it is thermalnoise-limited up to 50kHz.
To mitigate their effects, the first integrator employs CDS, and the entire modulator is chopped, as shown in Fig. 11.2.2.
Fig. 11.2.3 shows the spectrum of the decimated conversion result (104 samples, decimated with a sinc4 filter) in the CapDAC calibration mode with and without chopping.
To this end, a replica capacitive input network (shown in grey in Fig. 11.2.2) is also implemented.
As shown in Fig. 11.2.4, this is simply realized by adding two extra transistors to a gain-boosted folded-cascode fully differential amplifier.
As shown in Fig. 11.2.7, the CDC is fabricated in a standard 2P4M 0.35μm CMOS process and occupies an active area of 2.6mm2.
Fig. 11.2.5 provides a performance summary with comparison to other state-of-the-art capacitive sensor interfaces [2-6].
The small capacitance changes created by driving the shaker with a 100Hz square-wave are shown in Fig. 11.2.6.
